Subject: Renewal sync — upcoming contract & burst needs

Lukas,

Quick heads-up — our Q1 roadmap has a feature landing that will spike inference volume for 6–10 weeks starting mid-Nov. We're on track to exceed our current commit; before we jump in I wanted to check options for committing earlier vs. bursting.

High level ask: can we structure the renewal so we lock in a multi-year discount but have an "accelerated ramp" trigger that gives us temporary burst capacity (and a clear overage/pricing ladder) when usage goes above 140% of committed TPS for a rolling 7-day window? We're also trying to align the contract to fiscal year-end (Co-term to 2029-01-31).

We'd like a short call next week with pricing and someone who owns capacity. Priya is on the thread for procurement. Thanks —

— Sanjay
Director, Platform Engineering
Codeline Inc.

Sanjay — thanks for the heads-up. Short answer: yes, we can design the renewal to cover both a multi-year committed discount and a predictable oversubscribe/burst ladder. Proposed approach below; can discuss on a quick call (30m) next Tue.

Proposed structure (draft):
- 36-month base commitment (co-term to 2029-01-31, then annual anniversary) with tiered unit pricing at commit bands.
- Early-acceleration window: if usage >= 140% of monthly commit for any rolling 7-day window, temporary burst capacity is unlocked automatically for up to 30 days. Burst charged at pre-agreed oversubscribe ladder: 140–200% = +25% unit rate; 200–300% = +60% unit rate; >300% = on-demand rate.
- Optional true-up at quarter-end (customer chooses quarterly or annual true-up).
- Auto-renew enabled by default with 60-day opt-out notice to support budgeting.
- DocuSign amendment will include an "accelerated ramp" addendum and explicit capacity SLA for Dedicated pools.

For the call I'll bring pricing and marissa will cover billing/cutover. Karthik can speak to technical limits and burst placement. Proposed times: Tue Sep 4 10:00 or 14:00 PDT.

Thanks —

Lukas Meyer
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0183

Thanks Lukas — Tue 10am works for us. A couple of procurement clarifications before the call:
- We prefer quarterly true-up rather than annual.
- Need clarity on the billing cadence for burst charges (invoice within 30 days of end of burst window).
- We may request an early-termination credit if a major feature is delayed beyond Q2 2029 (procurement requirement).

Please add a short clause for early-termination credit range (pro-rated credit of remaining committed months) — amount to be discussed. Also confirm whether we can include a 90-day SLT (service level threshold) before burst auto-unlocks (operationally we'd like a short buffer).

— Priya
Sr. Procurement Manager, Codeline Inc.

Priya — good questions, following up after the internal sync. Answers and next steps:

1) Quarterly true-up: agreed, we'll include quarterly true-up in the amendment.

2) Billing cadence: burst overages will be invoiced monthly with a 30-day payment term. We can add a separate line item for oversubscribe usage to keep your committed spend line clean.

3) Early-termination credit: we can include a limited early-termination credit tied to a product delay clause (verified by roadmap milestone). Credit formula will be pro-rated remaining committed dollars, subject to a 6-month floor and max cap at 50% of remaining commitment. We'll draft options for the call.

4) 90-day SLT buffer: we prefer a 30-day operational buffer to avoid frequent oscillation; however, for enterprise customers we can support a configurable buffer parameter up to 90 days if requested. Recommend setting default to 30 and making 90 a negotiated option.

Next steps: Lukas will send an updated term sheet (v4) with the quarterly true-up, billing cadence language, and two early-termination credit formulas (conservative and customer-friendly). We'll include a DocuSign link for initial signature and flag the amendment for Dedicated pool SLA.

Action items: 
- Lukas: share v4 term sheet and DocuSign draft by EOD Fri 9/15.
- Marissa: prepare billing examples for 140%/220%/320% scenarios.
- Karthik: confirm Dedicated pool placement and expected latency impact for burst.

Thanks —

Marissa Cole
Director, Commercial Ops, Redwood Inference
